subproblem.title: Differentiation of radial cutoff integrals under the integral sign
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, ν a measure on ℝ^P (Euclid P), y ∈ ℝ^P, φ : ℝ → ℝ of class C¹ with φ(u) = 0 for every u ≥ A, where A > 0, q : ℝ^P → ℝ ν-a.e. strongly measurable with |q(x)| ≤ B for all x, and τ, R₀ ∈ ℝ with τ > 0, Aτ < R₀ and ν(B̄_{R₀}(y)) < ∞ (closed ball). Write r(x) := |x − y| (Euclidean norm) and φ' := deriv φ. Then (a) x ↦ φ(r(x)/τ)q(x) is ν-integrable; (b) x ↦ −(r(x)/τ²)φ'(r(x)/τ)q(x) is ν-integrable; and (c) the real function σ ↦ ∫ φ(r(x)/σ)q(x) dν(x) has derivative ∫ −(r(x)/τ²)φ'(r(x)/τ)q(x) dν(x) at σ = τ (HasDerivAt).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (ν : Measure (Euclid P)) (y : Euclid P) (φ : ℝ → ℝ) (q : Euclid P → ℝ) (A B τ R₀ : ℝ), ContDiff ℝ 1 φ → (∀ u, A ≤ u → φ u = 0) → 0 < A → 0 < τ → A * τ < R₀ → ν (closedBall y R₀) ≠ ∞ → AEStronglyMeasurable q ν → (∀ x, ‖q x‖ ≤ B) → Integrable (fun x => φ (‖x - y‖ / τ) * q x) ν ∧ Integrable (fun x => -(‖x - y‖ / τ ^ 2) * deriv φ (‖x - y‖ / τ) * q x) ν ∧ HasDerivAt (fun σ => ∫ x, φ (‖x - y‖ / σ) * q x ∂ν) (∫ x, -(‖x - y‖ / τ ^ 2) * deriv φ (‖x - y‖ / τ) * q x ∂ν) τ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Step 1 ("by differentiation under the integral sign I and J are C¹"; Simon Ch. 4, 3.4 and 3.16, where I(ρ) = ∫φ(r/ρ)dμ and J(ρ) are differentiated in ρ). Here the statement is proved for an arbitrary measure ν and an arbitrary bounded weight q, so that it covers I (q ≡ 1), the normal-weighted mass (q = |D^⊥r|²) and truncated weights.
Notation: r(x) := |x − y|, φ' := deriv φ, K := B̄_{R₀}(y) (closed ball), so ν(K) < ∞.
1. (φ and φ' vanish on [A, ∞).) For u > A, φ vanishes on the open interval (A, ∞) ∋ u, so φ'(u) = 0. Hence φ(u) = 0 for all u ≥ A and φ'(u) = 0 for all u > A. (At u = A one also has φ'(A) = 0, since φ is differentiable at A and φ(A + h) = 0 = φ(A) for h ≥ 0; this is not needed below.)
2. (Bounds.) φ and φ' are continuous because φ ∈ C¹. Put K₀ := 2R₀/τ > 0 and let C₀ := max_{[0,K₀]}|φ|, C₁ := max_{[0,K₀]}|φ'| (finite by compactness of [0, K₀]). Also B ≥ 0, since B ≥ |q(x)| ≥ 0 at any point x of ℝ^P.
3. (A neighbourhood of τ.) As A > 0 and Aτ < R₀ we have τ < R₀/A and R₀ > 0. Put δ := min(τ/2, (R₀/A − τ)/2) > 0. For σ in the open interval (τ − δ, τ + δ): σ > τ/2 > 0 and σ < R₀/A, i.e. Aσ < R₀.
4. (The integrands and their domination.) For σ > 0 and x ∈ ℝ^P put F(σ, x) := φ(r(x)/σ)q(x) and F'(σ, x) := −(r(x)/σ²)φ'(r(x)/σ)q(x). Let σ ∈ (τ − δ, τ + δ).
   (i) If x ∉ K then r(x) > R₀ > Aσ, so r(x)/σ > A and, by step 1, F(σ, x) = F'(σ, x) = 0.
   (ii) If x ∈ K then 0 ≤ r(x)/σ ≤ R₀/(τ/2) = K₀, so |φ(r/σ)| ≤ C₀, |φ'(r/σ)| ≤ C₁, and r/σ² ≤ R₀/(τ/2)²; hence |F(σ, x)| ≤ C₀B and |F'(σ, x)| ≤ L := (R₀/(τ/2)²)·C₁·B.
   Therefore |F(σ, x)| ≤ C₀B·1_K(x) and |F'(σ, x)| ≤ L·1_K(x) for all x and all σ ∈ (τ − δ, τ + δ). The functions C₀B·1_K and L·1_K are ν-integrable because ν(K) < ∞.
5. (Measurability; parts (a), (b).) For fixed σ > 0 the maps x ↦ φ(r(x)/σ) and x ↦ −(r(x)/σ²)φ'(r(x)/σ) are continuous (compositions of x ↦ |x − y|, division by σ, φ, φ'), hence strongly measurable; multiplied by the ν-a.e. strongly measurable q they give ν-a.e. strongly measurable functions F(σ, ·), F'(σ, ·). By step 4 with σ = τ, F(τ, ·) and F'(τ, ·) are dominated by integrable functions, hence ν-integrable. These are (a) and (b).
6. (Pointwise derivative.) Fix x. For σ > 0, σ ↦ r(x)/σ has derivative −r(x)/σ², and φ is differentiable everywhere, so by the chain rule σ ↦ F(σ, x) = φ(r(x)/σ)q(x) has derivative φ'(r(x)/σ)·(−r(x)/σ²)·q(x) = F'(σ, x) at every σ > 0, in particular at every σ ∈ (τ − δ, τ + δ).
7. (Differentiation under the integral sign; part (c).) Apply the dominated differentiation theorem (Mathlib hasDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_loc_of_deriv_le) with the neighbourhood (τ − δ, τ + δ) of τ: F(σ, ·) is a.e. strongly measurable for every σ (step 5); F(τ, ·) is integrable (step 5); F'(τ, ·) is a.e. strongly measurable (step 5); |F'(σ, x)| ≤ L·1_K(x) for all x and all σ in the neighbourhood, with L·1_K integrable (step 4); and σ ↦ F(σ, x) has derivative F'(σ, x) at each σ of the neighbourhood, for every x (step 6). The theorem yields that σ ↦ ∫F(σ, x)dν(x) has derivative ∫F'(τ, x)dν(x) at τ, which is (c). ∎

For σ in (τ − δ, τ + δ), δ = min(τ/2, (R₀/A − τ)/2), one has σ > τ/2 and Aσ < R₀, so F(σ,·) = φ(r/σ)q and F'(σ,·) = −(r/σ²)φ'(r/σ)q vanish off K = B̄_{R₀}(y).
On K both are bounded uniformly in σ; constant·1_K is ν-integrable since ν(K) < ∞, giving integrability (a), (b) and the domination.

subproblem.title: Radial first-variation identity for a varifold with generalized mean curvature
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P any set, R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep U n) with μ := R.measure = θHⁿ⌞M (Hⁿ = μHE[n]), W ⊆ U open, and H : ℝ^P → ℝ^P any map, such that x ↦ p_x is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, where p_x is the orthogonal projection onto T_xM := approxTangentPlane n M x, and R.firstVariation X = −∫⟨X, H⟩dμ for every C¹ compactly supported X : ℝ^P → ℝ^P with tsupport X ⊆ W. Let y ∈ ℝ^P and A, τ ∈ ℝ with τ > 0 and B̄_{Aτ}(y) ⊆ W (closed ball), and let φ : ℝ → ℝ be C¹ with φ(u) = 1 for u ≤ 1 and φ(u) = 0 for u ≥ A. Write r(x) := |x − y|, φ' := deriv φ and N(x) := |(x − y) − p_x(x − y)|²/|x − y|² (= 0 at x = y by 0/0 = 0). Then n∫φ(r/τ)dμ + ∫(r/τ)φ'(r/τ)(1 − N)dμ = −∫φ(r/τ)⟨x − y, H(x)⟩dμ (Bochner integrals).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U W : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n) (H : Euclid P → Euclid P), IsOpen W → W ⊆ U → AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x => (approxTangentPlane n R.carrier x).starProjection) R.measure → (∀ X : Euclid P → Euclid P, ContDiff ℝ 1 X → HasCompactSupport X → tsupport X ⊆ W → R.firstVariation X = -∫ x, inner ℝ (X x) (H x) ∂R.measure) → ∀ (y : Euclid P) (φ : ℝ → ℝ) (A τ : ℝ), ContDiff ℝ 1 φ → (∀ u, u ≤ 1 → φ u = 1) → (∀ u, A ≤ u → φ u = 0) → 0 < τ → closedBall y (A * τ) ⊆ W → (n : ℝ) * (∫ x, φ (‖x - y‖ / τ) ∂R.measure) + (∫ x, ‖x - y‖ / τ * deriv φ (‖x - y‖ / τ) * (1 - ‖(x - y) - (approxTangentPlane n R.carrier x).starProjection (x - y)‖ ^ 2 / ‖x - y‖ ^ 2) ∂R.measure) = -∫ x, φ (‖x - y‖ / τ) * inner ℝ (x - y) (H x) ∂R.measure
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Step 1 (the radial test field X_τ(x) = φ(r/τ)(x − y), its tangential divergence, and (MC) applied to X_τ) together with Preliminaries (P2)–(P4); Simon Ch. 4, 3.1–3.3 and 3.14/3.16.
Notation: r(x) := |x − y|, φ' := deriv φ, p_x the orthogonal projection onto T_xM := approxTangentPlane n M x, N(x) := |(x − y) − p_x(x − y)|²/r(x)² (N(y) = 0), K := B̄_{Aτ}(y), div_M X(x) := tangentialDivergence n M X x = trace(p_x ∘ DX(x)).
1. (The profile.) A > 1: otherwise A ≤ 1 and the hypotheses give both φ(A) = 1 and φ(A) = 0. For u > A, φ vanishes near u, so φ'(u) = 0; thus φ(u) = 0 for u ≥ A and φ'(u) = 0 for u > A. φ and φ' are continuous, so C₀ := max_{[0,A]}|φ| and C₁ := max_{[0,A]}|φ'| are finite.
2. (The test field.) Define X(x) := φ(r(x)/τ)(x − y).
   (a) On the open ball B(y, τ), r/τ < 1, so φ(r/τ) = 1 and X(x) = x − y; hence X agrees with x ↦ x − y on a neighbourhood of y, and DX(y) = I.
   (b) At x ≠ y the map z ↦ |z − y| is C^∞ near x (the Euclidean norm is smooth away from 0; Mathlib contDiffAt_norm) with derivative h ↦ ⟨(x − y)/r, h⟩. Hence X is C¹ near x and DX(x)h = φ(r/τ)h + τ⁻¹φ'(r/τ)⟨(x − y)/r, h⟩(x − y).
   (c) By (a) and (b), X is C¹ at every point, hence ContDiff ℝ 1 X. If X(x) ≠ 0 then φ(r/τ) ≠ 0, so r/τ < A by step 1; thus {X ≠ 0} ⊆ B(y, Aτ) and tsupport X ⊆ K ⊆ W. K is compact, so X has compact support. By hypothesis, R.firstVariation X = −∫⟨X, H⟩dμ.
3. (Right-hand side.) For every x, ⟨X(x), H(x)⟩ = φ(r/τ)⟨x − y, H(x)⟩. Equal integrands have equal Bochner integrals, so −∫⟨X, H⟩dμ = −∫φ(r/τ)⟨x − y, H(x)⟩dμ. No measurability or integrability of H is needed.
4. (First variation as a μ-integral, (P4).) By definition R.firstVariation X = ∫_M θ(x)·div_M X(x) dHⁿ(x), and μ = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ with θ = R.mult measurable and finite-valued. The withDensity formula ∫g d(λ.withDensity f) = ∫f(x).toReal·g(x) dλ (Mathlib integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul; it holds for every g, without integrability assumptions) gives R.firstVariation X = ∫div_M X dμ.
5. (Dimension of the tangent planes, (P3).) By IMRep.orients, for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x there is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q. For such x the existential in the definition of approxTangentPlane holds, so T_xM is a subspace Q' with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q', and dim T_xM = n (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.finrank_eq). Since μ ≪ Hⁿ⌞M (withDensity_absolutelyContinuous), dim T_xM = n for μ-a.e. x. For such x, trace p_x = n: writing p_x = ι∘π with π the orthogonal projection onto T_xM and ι the inclusion, trace(ι∘π) = trace(π∘ι) = trace(id_{T_xM}) = dim T_xM (LinearMap.trace_comp_comm').
6. (Divergence formula, Simon 3.2.) Let x satisfy dim T_xM = n and put p := p_x.
   If x = y: DX(y) = I by 2(a), so div_M X(y) = trace p = n = nφ(0) + (0/τ)φ'(0)(1 − N(y)) (φ(0) = 1).
   If x ≠ y: with a := φ(r/τ), b := τ⁻¹φ'(r/τ)/r, v := x − y, step 2(b) gives DX(x) = aI + b·(h ↦ ⟨v, h⟩v), so p∘DX(x) = a·p + b·(h ↦ ⟨v, h⟩pv) and trace(p∘DX(x)) = a·trace p + b⟨v, pv⟩ = na + b|pv|² (trace of a rank-one map h ↦ ⟨v, h⟩w is ⟨v, w⟩; ⟨v, pv⟩ = |pv|² because p is self-adjoint and idempotent). By Pythagoras (v − pv ⊥ pv), |pv|² = |v|² − |v − pv|² = r²(1 − N(x)). Hence div_M X(x) = nφ(r/τ) + τ⁻¹φ'(r/τ)·r·(1 − N(x)) = nφ(r/τ) + (r/τ)φ'(r/τ)(1 − N(x)).
   Consequently div_M X = n f₁ + f₂ μ-a.e., where f₁(x) := φ(r(x)/τ) and f₂(x) := (r(x)/τ)φ'(r(x)/τ)(1 − N(x)).
7. (Integrability, (P2).) K is compact with K ⊆ W ⊆ U, so μ(K) = ∫_{M∩K}θ dHⁿ < ∞ by IMRep.locallyIntegrable_mult. If x ∉ K then r/τ > A, so f₁(x) = f₂(x) = 0 by step 1. If x ∈ K then r/τ ∈ [0, A], so |f₁(x)| ≤ C₀ and, since 0 ≤ N ≤ 1 (|v − p_x v| ≤ |v| because v − p_x v is the orthogonal projection of v onto (T_xM)^⊥; Mathlib Submodule.starProjection_orthogonal_val, norm_starProjection_apply_le), |f₂(x)| ≤ A·C₁. f₁ is continuous. f₂ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable: x ↦ p_x(x − y) is obtained from the μ-a.e. strongly measurable operator-valued map x ↦ p_x (hypothesis) and the continuous map x ↦ x − y by the continuous evaluation (T, v) ↦ Tv (isBoundedBilinearMap_apply), and f₂ is built from it and continuous functions by continuous operations and division. Hence f₁, f₂ ∈ L¹(μ).
8. (Conclusion.) By steps 4, 6, 7 and linearity of the integral, R.firstVariation X = ∫div_M X dμ = ∫(n f₁ + f₂)dμ = n∫φ(r/τ)dμ + ∫(r/τ)φ'(r/τ)(1 − N)dμ. By steps 2(c) and 3, R.firstVariation X = −∫φ(r/τ)⟨x − y, H(x)⟩dμ. Combining the two expressions gives the identity. ∎

subproblem.title: Lower density bound at a point with an approximate tangent plane
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ with n ≥ 1, M ⊆ ℝ^P any set, x ∈ ℝ^P, and Q a linear subspace of ℝ^P that is an approximate tangent space of M at x in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, Def. 1.4 (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q: dim Q = n and ∫_{η_{x,ρ}(M)} f dHⁿ → ∫_Q f dHⁿ as ρ ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ), where η_{x,ρ}(z) = ρ⁻¹(z − x), Hⁿ = μHE[n], and the integrals are Bochner integrals for Hⁿ restricted to the indicated sets). Let ω_n := unitBallVolume n, the Lebesgue measure of the open unit ball of ℝⁿ. Then for every c ∈ [0, ∞] with c < ω_n there is ρ₀ > 0 such that c·ρⁿ ≤ Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) for every ρ ∈ (0, ρ₀), where B̄_ρ(x) is the closed ball (Lean: ∀ᶠ ρ in 𝓝[>] 0, c * ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n) ≤ μHE[n] (M ∩ closedBall x ρ)).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), 0 < n → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q → ∀ c : ℝ≥0∞, c < unitBallVolume n → ∀ᶠ ρ in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), c * ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n) ≤ μHE[n] (M ∩ closedBall x ρ)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Step 5(i), the comparison with the test function ψ₊ (1_{B̄_1(0)} ≤ ψ₊ ≤ 1_{B̄_{1+ε''}(0)}) which gives the lower density bound; Simon Ch. 3, 1.5(3), and Ch. 4, 4.10(1).
Notation: Hⁿ := μHE[n] on ℝ^P; η_ρ(z) := ρ⁻¹(z − x) (Chapter03.blowUpMap x ρ); ω_n := unitBallVolume n = volume(B_1(0) ⊆ ℝⁿ), ℝⁿ = Euclid n.
1. (Reduction.) Since n ≥ 1, ω_n is the volume of a bounded set, so ω_n < ∞; hence c < ω_n forces c < ∞. If c = 0 the claim is trivial. Otherwise treat c as a positive real. Since (1 + ε)ⁿ → 1 as ε ↓ 0 and c < ω_n, choose ε > 0 with c·(1 + ε)ⁿ < ω_n.
2. (Test function.) Let ψ(z) := max{0, min{1, (1 + ε − |z|)/ε}}. ψ is continuous, 0 ≤ ψ ≤ 1, ψ = 1 on B̄_1(0), and ψ = 0 outside B̄_{1+ε}(0); in particular ψ ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ).
3. (The limit integral is at least ω_n.) dim Q = n. Fix an orthonormal basis of Q; it yields a linear isometry j : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P with image Q (j = inclusion ∘ (basis representation)⁻¹). Hausdorff measure is invariant under isometries (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image), and on ℝⁿ, μHE[n] equals Lebesgue measure (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). Since j maps the open unit ball of ℝⁿ onto Q ∩ B_1(0), Hⁿ(Q ∩ B_1(0)) = volume(B_1(0) ⊆ ℝⁿ) = ω_n. Likewise Hⁿ⌞Q is finite on compact sets (pull back to ℝⁿ), so ψ is Hⁿ⌞Q-integrable. As ψ ≥ 0 and ψ = 1 on B_1(0): L := ∫_Q ψ dHⁿ ≥ ∫_{Q∩B_1(0)} ψ dHⁿ = Hⁿ(Q ∩ B_1(0)) = ω_n > c(1 + ε)ⁿ.
   By HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q applied to f = ψ, a(ρ) := ∫_{η_ρ(M)} ψ dHⁿ → L as ρ ↓ 0. Hence there is ρ₁ > 0 such that ofReal(a(ρ)) > c(1 + ε)ⁿ for all ρ ∈ (0, ρ₁).
4. (Upper bound for the blow-up integral.) Fix ρ > 0 and let λ := Hⁿ⌞η_ρ(M). Since ψ ≥ 0 is continuous, ∫ψ dλ = (∫⁻ofReal(ψ)dλ).toReal (integral_eq_lintegral_of_nonneg_ae; this holds whether or not ψ is λ-integrable), so ofReal(a(ρ)) ≤ ∫⁻ofReal(ψ)dλ (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal_le) ≤ λ(B̄_{1+ε}(0)) = Hⁿ(B̄_{1+ε}(0) ∩ η_ρ(M)), using ofReal(ψ) ≤ 1_{B̄_{1+ε}(0)}. Moreover B̄_{1+ε}(0) ∩ η_ρ(M) = η_ρ(B̄_{(1+ε)ρ}(x) ∩ M), and η_ρ is the translation z ↦ z − x (an isometry) followed by the homothety of ratio ρ⁻¹, so Hⁿ(η_ρ(S)) = ρ^{−n}Hⁿ(S) for every S ⊆ ℝ^P (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image, euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image). Therefore ofReal(a(ρ)) ≤ ofReal(ρ⁻¹)ⁿ·Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_{(1+ε)ρ}(x)).
5. (Conclusion.) For ρ ∈ (0, ρ₁), steps 3 and 4 give c(1 + ε)ⁿ ≤ ρ^{−n}Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_{(1+ε)ρ}(x)), i.e. c·((1 + ε)ρ)ⁿ ≤ Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_{(1+ε)ρ}(x)). Given ρ' ∈ (0, (1 + ε)ρ₁), apply this with ρ := ρ'/(1 + ε): c·ρ'ⁿ ≤ Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_{ρ'}(x)). Thus the claim holds with ρ₀ := (1 + ε)ρ₁; in filter form, the map ρ' ↦ ρ'/(1 + ε) tends to 0⁺ along 𝓝[>] 0, so the eventual statement transfers. ∎

Take a continuous compactly supported ψ with 1_{B̄_1(0)} ≤ ψ ≤ 1_{B̄_{1+ε}(0)}.
∫_Q ψ dHⁿ ≥ Hⁿ(Q ∩ B_1(0)) = ω_n (isometry ℝⁿ ≅ Q, μHE[n] = volume on ℝⁿ); the blow-up integrals converge to it.
ofReal(∫_{η_ρ(M)}ψ dHⁿ) ≤ Hⁿ(η_ρ(M) ∩ B̄_{1+ε}(0)) = ρ^{−n}Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_{(1+ε)ρ}(x)) (integral_eq_lintegral_of_nonneg_ae; Hausdorff scaling).
Reparametrise ρ' = (1 + ε)ρ.

Source: parent proof, Steps 1–2 (Simon Ch. 4, 3.4–3.5 and 3.16 with |H| ≤ κ). The parent integrates τ^{−n}J'(τ) over [s, t] and applies Tonelli; here, exactly as in Simon's own derivation of 3.5 ("by integration in 3.4"), the same estimate is obtained by comparing derivatives with G(τ) := ∫φ(r/τ)q dμ, whose increment G(t) − G(s) = ∫(φ(r/t) − φ(r/s))q dμ is the integrated Tonelli expression; the truncation q = N/max(s, r)ⁿ keeps G finite and coincides with r^{−n}N wherever ∂_τφ(r/τ) ≠ 0, τ ≥ s. The pointwise factors r^{−n} ≤ τ^{−n} ≤ Aⁿr^{−n} are those of the parent (Simon's printed 3.5 has them in reversed order).
Notation: B̄_ρ := B̄_ρ(y); r(x) := |x − y|; N(x) := |(x − y) − p_x(x − y)|²/r(x)² (N(y) = 0); φ' := deriv φ; c := Aκ; 'measurable' means μ-a.e. strongly measurable.
1. (Preliminaries.) κ ≥ |H(y)| ≥ 0, so c ≥ 0 (A > 1). 0 ≤ N ≤ 1 since |v − p_x v| ≤ |v| (v − p_x v is the orthogonal projection of v onto (T_xM)^⊥); N is measurable (x ↦ p_x(x − y) is measurable, as in radial_variation, step 7). B̄_{At} is compact and contained in the open set W, so there is δ₀ > 0 with B̄_{R₀} ⊆ W, R₀ := δ₀ + At (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open and cthickening_closedBall). B̄_{R₀} is a compact subset of U, so μ(B̄_ρ) ≤ μ(B̄_{R₀}) < ∞ for every ρ ≤ R₀ (IMRep.locallyIntegrable_mult).
2. (Profile.) Let φ(u) := Ψ((A − u)/(A − 1)), Ψ := Real.smoothTransition (C^∞, nondecreasing, 0 ≤ Ψ ≤ 1, Ψ = 0 on (−∞, 0], Ψ = 1 on [1, ∞)). Then φ is C¹, 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1, φ is nonincreasing, φ(u) = 1 for u ≤ 1 and φ(u) = 0 for u ≥ A. Hence φ' ≤ 0 everywhere; every u ≤ 1 is a global maximum point and every u ≥ A a global minimum point of φ, so φ'(u) = 0 there (IsLocalMax.deriv_eq_zero, IsLocalMin.deriv_eq_zero). Thus φ'(u) ≠ 0 implies 1 < u < A.
3. (Truncated weight.) q(x) := N(x)/max(s, r(x))ⁿ. Then 0 ≤ q ≤ s^{−n} and q is measurable. If r(x) > s then max(s, r) = r and q(x) = N(x)r^{−n} = |(x − y) − p_x(x − y)|²/r^{n+2} = F_y(x).
4. (Functions of the scale.) For τ > 0 let d_τ(x) := −(r(x)/τ²)φ'(r(x)/τ) ≥ 0 and define I(τ) := ∫φ(r/τ)dμ, G(τ) := ∫φ(r/τ)q dμ, I'(τ) := ∫d_τ dμ, G'(τ) := ∫d_τq dμ, J'(τ) := ∫d_τN dμ, h(τ) := ∫φ(r/τ)⟨x − y, H(x)⟩dμ. For τ ∈ [s, t] we have Aτ ≤ At < R₀ and μ(B̄_{R₀}) < ∞, so cutoff_deriv (with ν = μ and R₀, applied to the weights 1 (B = 1), q (B = s^{−n}) and N (B = 1)) gives: φ(r/τ), φ(r/τ)q, d_τ, d_τq and d_τN are μ-integrable, I has derivative I'(τ) at τ, and G has derivative G'(τ) at τ.
5. (The identity (E).) For τ ∈ [s, t], B̄_{Aτ} ⊆ B̄_{At} ⊆ W and φ satisfies the hypotheses of radial_variation, which gives nI(τ) + ∫(r/τ)φ'(r/τ)(1 − N)dμ = −h(τ). Pointwise (r/τ)φ'(r/τ)(1 − N) = (−τ)·d_τ + τ·d_τN (because τ·(r/τ²) = r/τ), and both terms are integrable, so ∫(r/τ)φ'(r/τ)(1 − N)dμ = −τI'(τ) + τJ'(τ). Hence
   (E) nI(τ) − τI'(τ) + τJ'(τ) = −h(τ) for τ ∈ [s, t].
6. (Mean curvature term.) Fix τ ∈ [s, t]. If φ(r(x)/τ) ≠ 0 then r(x) < Aτ, so |φ(r/τ)⟨x − y, H(x)⟩| ≤ φ(r/τ)·r·κ ≤ cτ·φ(r/τ); if φ(r/τ) = 0 both sides vanish. Since cτφ(r/τ) is integrable, |h(τ)| ≤ cτI(τ) (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le). Equivalently −cI(τ) ≤ h(τ)/τ ≤ cI(τ).
7. (Comparison (C), Simon 3.5.) J'(τ) ≥ 0 because d_τ ≥ 0 and N ≥ 0. For τ ∈ [s, t] and every x: d_τq ≤ τ^{−n}d_τN ≤ Aⁿd_τq. Indeed, if φ'(r/τ) = 0 all three terms vanish; otherwise 1 < r/τ < A by step 2, so s ≤ τ < r < Aτ, max(s, r) = r, q = N r^{−n}, and τ ≤ r ≤ Aτ gives r^{−n} ≤ τ^{−n} ≤ Aⁿr^{−n}; multiply by d_τN ≥ 0. Integrating (all three functions are integrable):
   (C) G'(τ) ≤ τ^{−n}J'(τ) ≤ AⁿG'(τ) for τ ∈ [s, t].
8. (Exponentially weighted ratios, Simon 3.16.) For b ∈ {c, −c} put Φ_b(τ) := e^{bτ}·τ^{−n}·I(τ). For τ ∈ [s, t], the product rule, step 4 and (τ^{−n})' = −nτ^{−n−1} give that Φ_b has derivative Φ_b'(τ) = e^{bτ}(bτ^{−n}I + τ^{−n}I' − nτ^{−n−1}I). By (E), τ^{−n}I' − nτ^{−n−1}I = τ^{−n−1}(τI' − nI) = τ^{−n−1}(τJ' + h) = τ^{−n}J' + τ^{−n}(h/τ), so
   Φ_b'(τ) = e^{bτ}τ^{−n}J'(τ) + e^{bτ}τ^{−n}(bI(τ) + h(τ)/τ).
   (a) b = c: cI + h/τ ≥ 0 by step 6, e^{cτ} ≥ 1 (c ≥ 0, τ > 0) and τ^{−n}J' ≥ 0, so Φ_c'(τ) ≥ e^{cτ}τ^{−n}J'(τ) ≥ τ^{−n}J'(τ) ≥ G'(τ) by (C).

   (K2) 1_{B̄_t∖B̄_{As}}F_y ≤ (φ(r/t) − φ(r/s))q pointwise: on B̄_t∖B̄_{As}, r ≤ t gives φ(r/t) = 1, r > As gives r/s > A and φ(r/s) = 0, and r > As > s gives q = F_y (step 3); elsewhere the left side is 0 while φ(r/t) − φ(r/s) ≥ 0 (r/t ≤ r/s and φ nonincreasing) and q ≥ 0.
   (K3) (φ(r/t) − φ(r/s))q ≤ 1_{B̄_{At}∖B̄_s}F_y pointwise: if r ≤ s, both φ-values equal 1; if r > At, both vanish (then also r/s > A); otherwise x ∈ B̄_{At}∖B̄_s, q = F_y and φ(r/t) − φ(r/s) ≤ 1.
   F_y is measurable and 0 ≤ F_y ≤ s^{−n} on {r > s} (there F_y = q), and the annuli B̄_t∖B̄_{As}, B̄_{At}∖B̄_s are contained in {r > s} and have finite measure, so F_y is integrable on them. subproblem.title: Unit lower bound for the monotone ball ratio at support points
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ with n ≥ 1, U ⊆ ℝ^P any set, R = (M, θ, ξ) an IMRep U n with μ := R.measure = θHⁿ⌞M (Hⁿ = μHE[n]), W ⊆ U open, and κ ≥ 0. Suppose that the exponentially weighted ball ratio is monotone in W: for every z ∈ ℝ^P and 0 < s < t with B̄_t(z) ⊆ W, e^{κs}s^{−n}μ(B̄_s(z)) ≤ e^{κt}t^{−n}μ(B̄_t(z)) in [0, ∞] (closed balls; coefficients via ENNReal.ofReal). Then for every y ∈ spt μ (R.measure.support) and t > 0 with B̄_t(y) ⊆ W: ω_n ≤ e^{κt}t^{−n}μ(B̄_t(y)), where ω_n = unitBallVolume n.

1. (Facts about μ.) (a) For every Borel set S, μ(S) = ∫⁻_{M∩S}θ dHⁿ ≥ Hⁿ(M ∩ S), because θ = R.mult is a positive integer, hence ≥ 1, on M (IMRep.mult_pos). By IMRep.orients and Hⁿ⌞M(ℝ^P ∖ M) = 0, Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x lies in G; since μ ≪ Hⁿ⌞M (withDensity), μ(ℝ^P ∖ G) = 0.
2. (Contradiction hypothesis.) Fix y ∈ spt μ and t > 0 with B̄_t(y) ⊆ W, and suppose f_y(t) < ω_n.
3. (A slightly larger ball.) B̄_t(y) is compact and W is open, so B̄_{t+δ₀}(y) ⊆ W for some δ₀ > 0 (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open, cthickening_closedBall), and μ(B̄_{t+δ₀}(y)) < ∞ by 1(b). Fix m such that, with δ := δ₀/(m + 1) ∈ (0, δ₀], b := ofReal(e^{κt}/tⁿ)·μ(B̄_{t+δ}(y)) < ω_n, and choose c ∈ [0, ∞] with b < c < ω_n.
4. (No good point near y.) Let x ∈ G with |x − y| < δ and let Q be an approximate tangent space of M at x. Then B̄_t(x) ⊆ B̄_{t+δ}(y) ⊆ W. By tangent_lower_density (n ≥ 1, c < ω_n), c·σⁿ ≤ Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_σ(x)) for all sufficiently small σ > 0; fix such a σ with 0 < σ < t.
